The sampled orthogonal basis 1, u, u²−mean(u²) gives the exact signed differences in (1); taking absolute column sums gives the attained norm. Independently formed D X(XᵀX)⁻¹Xᵀ H in rational arithmetic for n=3,…,22 (230 jump columns); all entries and the displayed small norms agreed. Directly from (1), at t=k/n the columns converge uniformly to 6t(1−t) times the integral on [0,1] of |1+5(2t−1)(2x−1)|: the absolute-value integrands are uniformly Lipschitz and the discrete factors differ uniformly by O(1/n). For a=5|2t−1| this integral is 1 if a≤1 and (a+1/a)/2 otherwise. On the latter branch put z=|2t−1|; the stationary equation is 75z⁴−24z²+1=0. The two interior roots, branch endpoints, and the test t=1/4 give the unique maximizing pair. Density and the strict maximum gap away from this pair establish localization of every maximizing index sequence. n=3 is the identity case.
